clue.text: Unskilled in exercise involving piano

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: involving means the word for exercise wraps round the musical abbreviation

parts.note: to exercise a power is to exert it
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A hopeless pianist is told their keyboard practice shows little skill.
explanation.walkthrough: The page printed 'piano', which the scan's OCR misread; P is the musical marking for soft playing, a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert is skilled, so the prefix of negation gives someone lacking skill.

clue.text: New suit worn by politician with energy and motivation

indicators.note: worn by means the rearranged suit letters are put on round the politician and energy, like clothing
New signals that the letters of suit are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A politician in a new suit feels full of energy and drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn by' reads like clothing on the politician, but here the reshuffled suit letters are what is worn round him.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the driving force or stimulus behind an action, a synonym of motivation.

clue.text: Woman carrying tot consumes a foreign dish

indicators.note: carrying means the woman's name holds the rest inside it, as a mother holds a child

parts.note: Ena is a woman's name

indicators.note: consumes means the word for tot swallows the letter given by a

parts.note: a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A mother with a toddler on her hip tucks into some exotic food.
explanation.walkthrough: Two nested containers: 'consumes' acts first inside the tot, then 'carrying' wraps the woman's name round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican tortilla dish, food from abroad to an English solver.

clue.text: Sanctimonious rascal building canoe

parts.note: pi is an informal word for pious or sanctimonious
a rogue is a rascal

explanation.surface: A self-righteous scoundrel is busy making a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ca nee' as printed is an OCR slip for 'canoe'; 'building' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirogue is a dugout boat, a kind of canoe used in the Caribbean and Louisiana.

clue.text: Feels indignant about inmates I'd abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means the letters from I'd are left out of the word for inmates

parts.note: residents are the inmates of a house or institution
taken as written, with the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone is angry about prisoners who left them behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ID from RESIDENTS leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel bitter or aggrieved over it.

clue.text: Grain placed beside river for birds

parts.note: gr is the abbreviation for grain, the small unit of weight
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: Seed is scattered by a riverbank to feed the birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placed beside' is a link joining the two pieces side by side. The OUSE is a river in Yorkshire (and another in Sussex).
explanation.definitionFit: Grouse are game birds hunted on British moors; the plural is the same as the singular.

clue.text: Regular manoeuvres involving the Italian freedom fighter

indicators.note: involving means the rearranged letters surround the Italian article
manoeuvres signals the letters of regular are moved about into a new order

parts.note: il is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: Regular troops on exercise encounter an Italian resistance fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular' looks like a description of soldiers, but it is the anagram fodder, and 'manoeuvres' is its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerrilla is an irregular fighter, often one waging an insurgent war for liberation.

clue.text: Summarise features of dated range of goods

parts.note: out means out of fashion, dated
a line is a range of products in a shop

explanation.surface: Someone sums up what is notable about an old-fashioned product range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'features of' joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To outline a plan is to give its main points briefly, a synonym of sum up.

clue.text: Gently cutting second facet of glittering ornament

indicators.note: cutting means the musical letter for gently cuts into the other pieces

parts.note: an angle is a facet or aspect of a matter
p, piano, is the musical direction to play softly or gently

explanation.surface: A jeweller gently cuts another facet on a sparkling ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' puts P between S and ANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A spangle is a small shiny disc sewn on clothing to glitter, a sequin.

clue.text: Nark comprehends minds of rogues

indicators.note: comprehends in its sense of includes means the word for nark holds the word for minds

parts.note: to nark is to annoy, to pique
to mind is to care

explanation.surface: A police informer understands how criminals think.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nark' looks like a noun, the police informer, but here it is the British verb meaning to annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Picaresque fiction follows the adventures of a roguish hero, so it concerns rascals.

clue.text: Players taking meal before start of match

parts.note: tea is a light afternoon or evening meal

indicators.note: start of means only the first letter of match is taken

explanation.surface: Footballers have their tea before kick-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A team is a group of players on one side.

clue.text: Going backwards and forwards donating gin for distribution

indicators.note: distribution signals the letters of the preceding words are dealt out into a new order

explanation.surface: Gin is handed out to people as gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distribution' rearranges all fourteen letters of DONATING GIN FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Toing and froing is the idiom for repeated movement one way and then the other.

clue.text: Members required on, board to maintain balance

definitions.text: Members required on, board to maintain balance

parts.words: Members required on, board to maintain balance
parts.note: the members are limbs, and the board is a ship's deck: a sailor's ability to stay upright on a rolling vessel

explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' tempts as committee members of a board, but they are a sailor's limbs on board ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea legs are the ability to keep one's footing on a moving ship.

clue.text: Old man's earthenware jug

definitions.meaning: a large stoneware jug for spirits, also called a bellarmine

explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an aged fellow and a big stoneware bottle with a bearded face moulded on it.

clue.text: Swindled like Lincoln, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a Lincoln is a breed of long-wool sheep, which gets shorn

explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln suggests the president, but here it is the Lincoln Longwool sheep breed; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece is both to cheat someone and to shear a sheep of its wool.

clue.text: Subtle reasoning novelist displayed about Scottish island

indicators.note: about means the novelist's name goes round the other letters

parts.note: Joyce Cary was an Anglo-Irish novelist
S is an abbreviation for Scottish
Uist is an island in the Outer Hebrides

explanation.surface: A writer shows off clever arguments set on a Hebridean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed' is a link word. Joyce Cary wrote The Horse's Mouth; Uist is in the Hebrides off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Casuistry is clever but unsound argument, especially on moral questions.

clue.text: Gained pound, initially, like my friend at the bar

definitions.text: like my friend at the bar

indicators.note: initially means the letter for pound is placed at the beginning

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra
earned means gained by work

explanation.surface: Someone first put on weight, much like a barrister friend.
explanation.walkthrough: In court a barrister refers to a colleague as 'my learned friend'; 'the bar' is the legal profession, not a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Barristers call each other 'my learned friend', so a scholarly epithet fits the bar.

clue.text: Blow up, with greater negative result

definitions.text: Blow up, with greater negative result

parts.words: Blow up, with greater negative result
parts.note: in photography a negative is printed at a bigger size, so the result is greater

explanation.walkthrough: 'negative' suggests something bad, but it is the photographic negative.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up a photograph is to make it larger.

clue.text: Food taken in for a violinist

indicators.note: taken in means the answer is held inside the words for a violinist

explanation.surface: Someone takes a meal to a hungry fiddler.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are small filled pasta parcels.

clue.text: It's endlessly used by fellers hoping for a good cut

definitions.text: It's endlessly used by fellers hoping for a good cut

parts.words: It's endlessly used by fellers hoping for a good cut
parts.note: the endless loop of toothed steel is used by tree cutters and woodworkers

explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' looks like 'all the time', but this tool's blade is a continuous loop; 'fellers' is people felling trees, not chaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A band saw has a blade that is a continuous band running over wheels.

clue.text: On which we burn wood within radius, say

indicators.note: within means the first pieces are set inside the bone

parts.note: the radius is a bone of the forearm, one example of a bone
fir is a softwood timber

explanation.surface: A recipe of sorts: put wood on and the fire will take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radius, say' looks like geometry, but the radius is one of the forearm bones.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonfire is a large outdoor fire built for burning rubbish or for celebration.

clue.text: Less pleasant wine imbibed by northern king

indicators.note: imbibed by means the wine is drunk by, so set inside, the other letters

parts.note: ER, Edwardus Rex, is the royal cipher of a King Edward
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A king of the north grows meaner after drinking wine.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is usually the Queen, but it serves for a king too, as Edward's royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastier means more unpleasant.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing existed to really enjoy life, primarily

parts.note: was is the past of be, to exist

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter of each of the following four words is used

explanation.surface: A layabout lived only to have a good time.
explanation.definitionFit: A wastrel is an idle spendthrift, a ne'er-do-well.

clue.text: Use personal craft to ensure survival

definitions.text: Use personal craft to ensure survival

parts.words: Use personal craft to ensure survival
parts.note: getting by on one's own cunning and cleverness rather than steady means

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to survive by cleverness or cunning, with no regular income.

clue.text: Spirit barmen originally served before port

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of barmen is taken

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Bar staff first pour spirits, then the port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests drink alongside barmen and port, but it means liveliness.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is vigour and liveliness.

clue.text: Management leader is trained specially to do this

definitions.text: Management leader is trained specially to do this

indicators.note: specially signals the letters are put into a special new order
leader means the first letter of management is used

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A head of management is trained to run things.
explanation.walkthrough: M with IS and TRAINED is rearranged; the whole clue also describes what a manager is taught.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer is to manage or run affairs, which a trained head of management does.

clue.text: Backing husband elected in plot

indicators.note: in means husband and elected sit inside the word for plot

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot
in means elected, as a party in power

explanation.surface: A husband is chosen as part of a conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' tempts as a scheme, but it is a garden bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be behind someone is to support them.

clue.text: Selling fish consumed by bishop and others

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: consumed by means the fish is eaten, so placed inside, by the other letters

parts.note: et al is Latin for and others
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A bishop and friends eat fish they bought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Selling' means selling out, as in betraying someone, not trading.
explanation.definitionFit: Selling someone out is treachery, giving them up for gain.
